questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Infrastructure: The Engine of Development' refers to.
questions.a: Infrastructure is the vast network of tangible structures and systems a country runs on, roads, ports, power plants, telephone lines and telecom towers; it is the engine that pulls development forward.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Infrastructure: The Engine of Development'.
questions.a: Infrastructure is the economy's skeleton: goods, power and messages move only as well as the network allows.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Infrastructure: The Engine of Development' taught, and from which source text?
Explain in your own words what 'Roads, Railways and Metro Systems' refers to.
questions.a: Transport infrastructure carries people and goods: India's expanding network of national highways, over 68,000 km of railway tracks among the world's longest, and metro trains now running in 23 Indian cities.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Roads, Railways and Metro Systems'.
questions.a: Distance shrinks when roads, rails and metros grow: markets widen and journeys shorten.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Roads, Railways and Metro Systems' taught, and from which source text?
Explain in your own words what 'Energy and Digital Infrastructure' refers to.
questions.a: Power plants and grids light homes and run factories, while telephone lines, towers and optical fibre carry voices and data; energy and digital networks together multiply what every other sector can do.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Energy and Digital Infrastructure'.
questions.a: Electricity and connectivity are enablers: a clinic, a school and a factory all stand still without them.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Energy and Digital Infrastructure' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Energy and telecom (source: gees207.txt, Energy and telecom)

concepts.title: Infrastructure and the Quality of Life

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Infrastructure and the Quality of Life' refers to.
questions.a: APJ Abdul Kalam's dream of a developed India wants the same roads, power, water and communication in village and city; the chapter's graphs of railways, ports and metro length show infrastructure raising living standards.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Infrastructure and the Quality of Life'.
questions.a: Development is measured in access: when village and city share the same infrastructure, opportunity spreads.
